publication_year_note: Issue running header on even pages prints 'Vol 25 No 1 April 2013' (primary journal volume/issue publication year: 2013), while Page 1 prints 'Copyright © 2012 International Institute for Environment and Development (IIED).' alongside DOI 10.1177/0956247812465803 (note: bibliographic header listed DOI 10.1177/0956247811418734, whereas the cached PDF matches the exact author and title with DOI 10.1177/0956247812465803).
rationale: This 16-page article is an ethnographic/grounded-theory qualitative case study of informal land allocation and water supply regulation in an inner-city informal settlement ('Boshoti') in Dhaka, Bangladesh, conducted via unstructured interviews, theoretical sampling, and participant observation over nine months between 2008 and 2011. It contains zero tables, zero regression models, zero hypothesis tests, and zero uncertainty measures (no SEs, CIs, t-stats, chi-square tests, or p-values), reporting only qualitative narratives and approximate descriptive figures (e.g., ~85% of room clusters having informal in-house water connections and informal vendor prices 10–28 times the official DWASA rate). Flagging it as eligible for quantitative synthesis is overstated.
